_readme: HOW TO USE: copy this file to server-config.json (same folder) and fill in your keys.
server-config.json is NEVER committed to git. Since v89 the keys stay on the
server and are attached to API calls by the /api/* proxies — browsers only
ever see capability flags, never the keys themselves.
Lines starting with _ are just notes; the server ignores them.
_section_server: Port the home server listens on.
_section_hardcover: Hardcover token — series info, content warnings, moods. Free token: hardcover.app → Account settings → API.
_section_google_books: Google Books API key — personal quota of 1,000 requests/day (the shared anonymous quota can run out). Get one: Google Cloud Console → enable the 'Books API' → Credentials → Create an API key (restrict it to the Books API).
_section_supabase: Supabase — optional cloud sync. Supabase dashboard → Project Settings → API.
_section_trope_inference: Trope inference (v152) — LLM trope tagging. The key stays on the server and is attached by the /api/trope-infer proxy; browsers only see a configured/missing flag. Any OpenAI-compatible provider works.
_trope_provider_note: One of: openrouter, gemini, groq, ollama, custom. (Ollama/custom need trope_base_url.)
_trope_model_note: Model id for the provider above. Free OpenRouter options that worked in testing: nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free, qwen/qwen3.8-27b:free, google/gemma-4-31b-it:free.
_trope_api_key_note: OpenRouter: openrouter.ai → Keys. Gemini/Groq: their dashboards. Ollama/local: anything non-empty (or leave provider unset).
_trope_base_url_note: Optional override. Needed for provider=custom (e.g. http://your-host:11434/v1). Leave empty to use the provider default.
